html:
A general strike and mass protest in Ouagadougou on 3 January 1966, led by trade unions against the austerity and one-party rule of President Maurice Yameogo, which brought the army to power.

Yameogo, president since independence in 1960, had cut wages while his circle lived well. Crowds called on the army to take over, and its chief, Sangoule Lamizana, did, ruling until 1980. It was among the first times in independent Africa that a popular movement brought down a president. Unions and students stayed a strong force in Upper Volta, and the same pattern recurred in the 2014 uprising. See also Upper Volta and Thomas Sankara.
sum: A general strike and mass protest in Ouagadougou on 3 January 1966, led by trade unions against the austerity and one-party rule of President Maurice Yameogo, which brought the army to power.
